title: Frag-storm: KV leak + allocator thrash causing GPU OOMs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Lina Chen
description: High-severity customer escalations observed across Hosted, Dedicated and Private clusters: frequent GPU OOM spikes correlated with large eviction/compaction activity in the prefix/KV cache. Symptoms: sudden session terminations, sustained allocator thrash and fragmentation (rapid growth of small free slabs), and kv-handle leaks that prevent reclamation. Multiple tenants reported degraded tail latency and token failures under sustained parallel loads. This ticket tracks triage, temporary mitigations, root cause fix, and rollout of a runtime patch.
impact_summary: Multiple paying customers (hosted & dedicated) experienced request failures and elevated 95/99 latency during peak traffic windows. Two dedicated tenants reported capacity exhaustion requiring manual intervention. Customer impact classified as high (data plane availability & reliability).
investigation_summary:
- Correlated memory metrics (GPU resident + host allocator fragmentation) with KV cache churn windows using dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood-inference.com/d/runtime/memory-oom
- Heap histograms show increasing counts of small free blocks (<8KB) while total free pool decreased.
- KV index scans show growth of 'stale handle' markers preventing slot reuse.
- Repro load: synthetic parquet prompt flood with 400 concurrent sessions reproduces OOM in ~6-8 minutes on a 16GB GPU worker.
- Heap profiler captured interleaved patterns: deferred_free() calls were being deferred by compaction worker and occasionally skipped due to cancellation race.
- Live trace points show an eviction storm triggered bloom-filter expansion when prefix cache exceeded bucket threshold.
root_cause: A race between the async prefix-cache bloom expansion and the allocator's deferred-free path can leave KV handles in a limbo state (marked stale but not reclaimed). Over time this produces a large population of tiny fragmented free regions plus linear growth of KV tombstones, which increases GPU memory pressure and prevents contiguous allocations, culminating in GPU OOMs. The problem is amplified by high concurrency (coldstart-heavy workloads) and by a fallback code path that defers reclamation when the eviction worker is overloaded.
temporary_mitigations: Rollback to previous bloom expansion threshold (config change) — reduced expansion aggressiveness in hosted tier (applied 2026-02-26)
Force synchronous reclaim on eviction for high-priority tenants as emergency measure (runtime flag) — documented and enabled for two affected dedicated clusters (2026-02-27)
Short-term rate limit on concurrent cold-start requests via API gateway route blacklist for susceptible models (applied 2026-02-28)
Provisioned burst buffers for the most impacted dedicated tenants (manual scaling)
permanent_fix_plan: 1) Fix deferred-free race: add handshake/sequence validation between bloom expansion and deferred_free path so a handle flip is atomic from allocator view
2) Compacting allocator enhancement: coalesce tiny free slabs opportunistically during low CPU/IO periods to reduce fragmentation
3) KV tombstone reclamation: background sweeper to accelerate reuse of stale handles with bounded IO impact
4) Add unit+stress tests that deterministically trigger the bloom expansion + eviction overlap to prevent regressions
5) Backfill canary automation and memory regressions gate in CI for runtime-1.19
rollout_plan: Create runtime-1.19-hotfix branch with estimator fixes. Stage: canary on non-critical hosted pool (48h), then staggered rollout to hosted primary, dedicated (low risk first), then private customers via upgrade bundle. If any canary shows >2% increase in tail allocation failures, rollback. Expected rollout window: 2026-03-15 -> 2026-03-19.
testing_notes:
- Unit tests added for deferred-free handshake.
- End-to-end stress test in perf lab (400 sessions, randomized KV sizes) shows reproduction suppressed from 6-8min to no failure in 2h run.
- Memory regression suite run against top 20 models passed.
- QA: integration with dedicated autoscaler validated on staging cluster (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621).
